title: What the site may and must not say about the chemicals in the air when idling-scooter fumes can be smelled
status: ESTIMATE (推估), signed after three sceptic reviews (corrections.md)
numbersFrom: results-smell.json (smell-chemicals step) and, for the benzene stay-through, the signed research/simulation/statements.json

alwaysCarry.zh: 推估，不是實測。數字都有範圍。這是機車另外加進空氣裡的量，不含原本街上的空氣。
alwaysCarry.en: Estimate, not a measurement. Every number has a range. These are amounts the scooters add to the air already there.
plus: the low-high range next to every number
the condition (case, wind, distance, height) and how often it happens
'shares come from older uncatalysed or carburetted engines; modern catalysed scooters may differ' on any view that names a chemical

may.strength: the strongest honest sentence of the kind the owner asked for
may.zh: 聞到的不是苯，但苯跟著一起來。只要你聞得到身旁怠速機車的廢氣，同一口空氣裡就有苯（推估）。
may.en: What you smell is not benzene, but benzene comes with it. Whenever you can smell the exhaust of the idling scooters beside you, the same breath of air holds benzene (estimate).
may.basis: Odour and every chemical come from the same exhaust fraction in the model (METHOD-SMELL 1, 5). Benzene stays far below its own odour threshold of 2,700 ppb: no pack draw reaches it. Benzene share of THC 1.2 / 2.7 / 5 %, from idle measurements in Taiwan, India and Nepal (moderate confidence).
may.mustCarry: 推估 / Estimate. The condition: 'if the smell is the scooters' exhaust' (the smell can come from other sources). Always shown with statement 'no-smell-not-clean' in the same view.

may.zh: 如果你聞到的是身旁機車的廢氣，那口空氣裡也有苯、1,3-丁二烯、甲醛，還有甲苯、二甲苯等十幾種廢氣成分（推估）。
may.en: If what you smell is the exhaust of the scooters beside you, that air also holds benzene, 1,3-butadiene and formaldehyde, as well as toluene, xylenes and about ten other exhaust chemicals (estimate).
may.basis: speciation.json: twelve chemicals with measured shares in petrol-engine exhaust. Hydrogen cyanide may be named, now that its 1-h comparison is done (below 340 ug/m3 everywhere).
may.mustCarry: 推估 / Estimate. The 'if'. The shares come from older engines. When the chemicals are listed, order them by share of exhaust or alphabetically, never by hazard.

may.zh: 世界衛生組織的癌症研究機構（IARC）把苯、1,3-丁二烯、甲醛列為「確定會讓人致癌」的第1類。這是說「證據有多強」，不是說等一個紅燈會有多少風險。汽油引擎廢氣整體被列為第2B類（「可能致癌」）。
may.en: The World Health Organization's cancer agency (IARC) puts benzene, 1,3-butadiene and formaldehyde in Group 1, 'causes cancer in humans'. That describes how strong the evidence is, not the risk from waiting at one red light. Petrol-engine exhaust as a whole is Group 2B, 'possibly causes cancer'.
may.mustCarry: Always show the meaning of the groups and exhaust's own 2B together. This statement must be a separate sentence from any sentence about smell, and must not sit in the same sentence as any number.

may.zh: 剛好聞得到廢氣味的時候，苯大約是 2 到 15 ppb（十億分之 2 到 15），範圍約 0.4 到 60 ppb（推估）。
may.en: At the moment the exhaust is just noticeable, benzene is about 2 to 15 parts per billion (range about 0.4 to 60 ppb; estimate).
may.basis: results-smell.json threshold_level: benzene 1.7 ppb (6,800-fold threshold) and 15 ppb (800-fold); P5 0.4 ppb, P95 58 ppb; 10,000 single-scooter draws; independent of the flow.
may.mustCarry: 推估 / Estimate; the range; 'a typical value, not a minimum'; 'the two numbers come from two smell tests of car exhaust from 1967-70'; 'no official value exists for a few seconds, so it cannot be called high or low'. Both numbers always together, never one alone.

may.zh: 聞不聞得到，要看風。風從一群怠速機車吹向人行道時，一個紅燈大部分的時間都聞得到；在街道峽谷、風沿著街吹的時候，只有部分時間聞得到，很多紅燈根本聞不到（推估）。
may.en: Whether you can smell it depends on the wind. With the wind blowing from a group of idling scooters toward the pavement, it can be smelled for most of a red. In a street canyon with the wind along the street, only some of the time, and in many reds not at all (estimate).
may.basis: results-smell.json smellable_share: S1-from 0.5 m / 0.7 m: 76 % (range 0-97 %) with the 800-fold threshold and 97 % (83-99 %) with the 6,800-fold one; S1: 0-29 % central, many draws with none.
may.mustCarry: Both thresholds' figures if any percentage is shown; 'one simulated red per case'; 'wind held; at most about 1 in 8 peak-hour reds have that wind'; low to low-moderate confidence.

may.zh: 風從機車群吹過來的時候，在離最近一台機車半公尺、小孩鼻子的高度，聞得到的那幾秒裡，苯平均大約 30 ppb，範圍約 2 到 360 ppb（推估）。
may.en: With the wind blowing from the scooters, half a metre from the nearest one at a child's nose height, benzene averages about 30 ppb over the seconds you can smell it (range about 2 to 360 ppb; estimate).
may.basis: results-smell.json S1-from K d=0.5 h=0.7: 33 ppb (800-fold) and 27 ppb (6,800-fold); low 2.1, high 360; 1,000 of 1,000 draws smellable.
may.mustCarry: 推估 / Estimate; range; the condition (wind held from the scooters, at most about 1 in 8 peak-hour reds); the share of seconds smellable (76-97 %); 'no official value exists for a few seconds'. Never next to a 1-hour, yearly or lifetime value.

may.zh: 聞不到，不代表空氣乾淨。沒有味道的時候也可能有苯。一氧化碳沒有味道，微粒小到看不見。
may.en: No smell does not mean clean air. Benzene can be there when nothing can be smelled. Carbon monoxide has no smell, and particles are too small to see.
may.basis: results-smell.json: S1 0.5 m / 0.7 m at the 800-fold threshold, central share of smellable seconds 0 while benzene is present over the red (signed stats).
may.mustCarry: Required on any view that carries 'smell-comes-with-benzene' or 'what-is-in-it'.

may.zh: 只等一個紅燈，依我們的中間推估，這些化學物質都不會因此達到 30 分鐘或 1 小時的公共參考值。
may.en: Waiting through one red light does not, on its own, bring any of these chemicals to a 30-minute or 1-hour public reference level, in our central estimate.
may.basis: results-smell.json section (d): one-red contribution below every reference at the central value in all cases; above only in the worst case of the rare near-calm NF1-fine case.
may.mustCarry: 'In a rare near-calm case, standing half a metre downwind of one tailpipe, the worst case can reach them'; low confidence. Never rewrite this as 'safe'.

may.zh: 如果有人整個小時每個紅燈都待在路邊（例如攤販、警察、導護），而且風一直從機車那邊吹過來，機車加進來的苯推估會超過美國加州的 1 小時參考值。
may.en: For someone who stays at the kerb through every red for an hour (a vendor, a police officer, a crossing guard), with the wind from the scooters the whole time, the benzene the scooters add is estimated to be above California's 1-hour reference level.
may.basis: Signed research/simulation statements.json; reproduced here: S1-from 0.5 m / 0.7 m 62 ug/m3 (18-200) against 27 ug/m3.
may.mustCarry: Estimate; range (from below to several times above); the wind must be held for the whole hour (rare); the same simulated red every time; the reference was derived from a longer exposure; 'above a reference level is not proof of harm'; nothing about cancer. Do not add acrolein or formaldehyde to this sentence.

may.zh: 那個味道比較可能來自燃燒後產生的醛類，不是沒燒完的汽油（推估，只能估到數量級）。
may.en: The smell more likely comes from aldehydes formed by burning, not from unburnt petrol (estimate, order of magnitude only).
may.basis: results-smell.json ownOdourByCase: acetaldehyde above its 1.5 ppb detection threshold in 61-100 % of draws in every case; benzene never at its own threshold in pack cases; petrol vapour not modelled.
may.mustCarry: 'order of magnitude'; acetaldehyde's 'distinct awareness' level (560 ppb) is not reached in pack cases; say 'probably part of what you smell', never 'you smell acetaldehyde'.

may.zh: （只放在詳細表格）每種化學物質整個小時都待在路邊的推估平均值，跟它自己的 1 小時或 30 分鐘參考值比較。
may.en: (Detail table only.) For each chemical, the estimated 1-hour or 30-minute average for someone who stays through every red, against its own reference value of the same averaging time.
may.mustCarry: Per row: confidence (acrolein and naphthalene: car data only, very low, range assumed); case label and how often it occurs; NF1-fine rows labelled 'rare near-calm worst position (about 1 % of reds or fewer), likely to read high'; 'Taiwan indoor-air standard' and 'WHO odour-annoyance guideline (not a health limit)' wherever those are the reference; 'no public value of 1 hour or shorter' for ethylbenzene, n-hexane and naphthalene.

mustNot: 'When you smell scooter fumes you are breathing cancer-causing chemicals', 'the smell is benzene', or any sentence that puts 'smell' and 'causes cancer' together or makes the smell itself carcinogenic.

'One red light gives you cancer' or 'raises your cancer risk'; any cancer risk or 'extra cases' number for a red, a day or a commute; the WHO 'no safe level of benzene' next to any seconds-long or red value.
Any seconds-long or smellable-seconds level (2-15 ppb, about 30 ppb, highest seconds) set next to a 30-min, 1-h, 8-h, annual or lifetime value, or called 'x times the limit'.

'Benzene, butadiene and formaldehyde (Group 1)' without the meaning of the groups and without exhaust's own 2B; any list ordered by IARC group. Equally, 'exhaust is only possibly carcinogenic' without the components.
'You are smelling unburnt petrol, and petrol causes cancer (IARC 2025)'. Petrol vapour was not modelled; that Group 1 label is for the fuel.
'You smell acetaldehyde / formaldehyde / acrolein' as a finding, or quoting only the lower odour threshold's percentage.
'Wherever you stand, when you can smell it you breathe 4-50 ppb benzene', or any smellable-seconds level without the share of seconds, the number of draws and the condition beside it.
Any NF1-fine (near-calm, single tailpipe) number in a headline, share card, summary sentence or first screen; any 'pushchair height 0.5 m'.

'Acrolein is above the safe level' or any acrolein headline; 'formaldehyde exceeds Taiwan's standard' (it is an indoor standard); 'exceeds the WHO guideline' for toluene or styrene without 'odour-annoyance'.
'Harmful', 'dangerous', 'toxic dose' or 'poison' for any of these levels.
'If you can't smell it, the air is fine', or any wording that makes smell a safety test.
Any statement about the chemical levels of modern catalysed, fuel-injected scooters.
Any number without its low-high range and 推估 / estimate.
Any claim that the levels are the whole air at the kerb; they are what the scooters add.
